title: Vendor Layout Spillover: Does Adjacency Confound the Market-Day Effect on Sales?
one_line: Use instrumental-variable-like reasoning on sparse, non-random vendor placement to separate the causal effect of foot traffic (day-of-week) from locational advantage, where standard causal adjustment fails because treatment is spatially embedded.
self_assessment: Has legs: the tension between observational causal inference (built for independent units) and spatial-network data (where treatment and confounders are entangled by geography) forces a genuine methodological compromise that exposes the limits of covariate adjustment.

title: Temporal Hypergraph Collapse: Detecting Brood-Pattern Asymmetries via Time-Windowed Subgraph Isomorphism
one_line: Can we detect early colony disease spread by comparing observed nurse→brood contact networks against the null model of 'symmetric diffusion,' where the technique fails unless we collapse temporal hyperedges into directed time-lagged digraphs?
self_assessment: The seam is real: standard network analysis treats contacts as undirected snapshots, but brood disease propagation is causal (nurse→brood, not vice versa) and time-indexed; we must engineer directed lagged edges from temporal contact sequences. This forces explicit handling of the temporal asymmetry rather than applying off-the-shelf centrality.

title: Thrift Price Clusters Under Measurement Error: Can k-means recover categories when item descriptions are noisy proxies for condition?
one_line: Apply k-means clustering to price × text-derived condition features on thrift items, but force the algorithm to work with *deliberately degraded* condition labels (truncation, OCR-style noise) to test whether market-meaningful clusters emerge despite the feature being corrupted—revealing the tension between what clustering needs (clean features) and what thrift data supplies (sparse, error-prone metadata).
self_assessment: This has legs because the core tension (clustering assumes latent clean structure, but thrift pricing is driven by messy grading systems) forces a methodological compromise: either you admit the cluster labels don't align with ground truth, or you ask what structure survives *despite* noise—which is honest and uncommon in tutorial examples.

title: Beekeeper Log Variance Decay: Inferring Inspection Fatigue from NLP Coherence Drift
one_line: Does the *linguistic consistency* of beekeeper inspection logs degrade predictably over a season, and can that decay signal colony stress better than the explicit observations recorded?
self_assessment: This has legs: NLP on logs assumes static vocabulary/style, but beekeepers' logs naturally drift in precision, detail, and reference consistency as fatigue or attention shifts. That drift itself—measured as token-sequence entropy or semantic coherence within rolling windows—becomes a signal. The insight is that the *noise floor* of the writing is more stable and informative than the surface content.

title: Vendor Revenue Stability via Isolation Forest on Compositional Sales Data
one_line: Can isolation forest detect destabilized vendors by treating item-category revenue shares as a simplex, where traditional anomaly detection fails because it ignores the sum-to-one constraint that defines market behavior?
self_assessment: This has legs: the core insight is that anomaly detection on compositional data (proportions summing to 1) breaks standard distance metrics, and forcing iso-forest to work on the simplex requires either log-ratio transformation or a custom metric—revealing why anomalies in *budget allocation* across categories (not just total revenue) signal real vendor stress.

title: Trail Bottleneck Detection via Temporal Hypergraph Switching
one_line: Can we detect trail segments where hiker flow transitions from parallel to sequential (bottlenecks) by collapsing GPS trajectory hyperedges into time-lagged directed graphs, forcing the technique to handle continuous paths as discrete switching events?
self_assessment: This has genuine friction: standard graph_network_analysis assumes nodes and edges are pre-defined, but trail data arrives as continuous trajectories (hyperedges spanning many GPS points). The insight is that bottlenecks aren't structural—they're behavioral regime shifts in the *temporal* edge-formation process, requiring us to bin time windows and detect when the digraph transitions from high out-degree (parallel dispersal) to low out-degree (forced serialization). That modification is the technique, not window dressing.
